source_retrieval.review_date: 2025-01-27 footer last-reviewed date; version 6 dated 2026-09-16, with review as required.

findings.before: The numeric CrCl range between 59 and 60 was widened into the printed 50–59 dose recommendation. Some contradictory numeric/band pairs were not identified; a selected 50–59 band could still suggest 75% despite numeric CrCl ≥60.
findings.after: Only exact numeric 50–59 enters the percentage discussion. Values >59 and <60 require source-gap review; all contradictory less-than-50, 50–59 and at-least-60 pairs are identified. Independent low-clearance/dialysis omission remains active.
findings.limits: No rounding rule or universal dose is invented; full clinical/pharmacy interpretation remains required.

findings.before: Systemic steroid criterion was encoded, but requirement for other systemic immunosuppressive medication had no separate baseline branch.
findings.after: Explicit baseline requirement produces the source exclusion for pembrolizumab. Unconfirmed assessment phase prompts review; immunosuppression used after treatment for immune toxicity is not misclassified as a baseline exclusion.

source.section: Exclusions; drug interactions pp8/7 distinguish post-treatment immune management

findings.before: Current grade 3/4 endocrine toxicity with controlled=true could bypass the existing uncontrolled-endocrine hold.
findings.after: Withhold while reconciling grade/control. The continuation exception requires improvement to grade ≤2, appropriate hormone control and steroid taper. Hypothyroidism remains its separate source pathway.
findings.limits: A contradictory entry alone does not justify permanent discontinuation.

findings.before: The current source renal-impairment caution for uracil-based DPD phenotype was present in the PDF but not assessable as a specific decision-tool pathway.
findings.after: A phenotype-only result with moderate/severe kidney impairment triggers review and genotype consideration before a fluorouracil starting dose; known complete deficiency remains a contraindication.
findings.limits: No numerical renal cutoff or DPD dose percentage is inferred. The older 00706 version 3 does not state this caveat; it is not silently attributed to that document.

findings.before: A recovered numerical rash grade could display a recurrence-based restart dose even while the same reaction was explicitly marked intolerable.
findings.after: Known intolerability suppresses those dose rows and retains a hold with a recovery-conflict explanation. Recurrence, ≤2-week interval, recovery and prior-dose safeguards remain.

source.supplement: Erbitux EMA SmPC section4.4 page6: intolerable/severe skin toxicity requires interruption

domains.checked: Head/neck and nasopharyngeal schedules use six weekly 40 mg/m² doses with concurrent radiotherapy. Cervical indications use five weekly doses with further concurrent doses at Consultant discretion. Radiotherapy follows cisplatin; cancel/postpone cisplatin when same-day radiotherapy is cancelled. Hydration and electrolytes follow the source and local policy.

ECOG 0–2; significant hearing impairment/tinnitus, pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypersensitivity and pre-existing renal impairment are exclusions. Baseline FBC, renal and liver profiles; audiology/creatinine clearance when clinically indicated. Repeat bloods before each cycle; disease monitoring follows the individual treatment plan.

ANC <1 or platelets <100: delay. CrCl 40–49: 50% of original cisplatin; 50–59: 75%; <40: not recommended. Haemodialysis: 50% may be considered by specialists. Fractional printed-band gaps require interpretation. Grade 2 neuropathy: reduce by 25%; grade 3/4: omit. No hepatic adjustment is expected.

00385.conclusion: Existing v0.84.45 numeric rules retained after fresh-source repeat audit and boundary testing; no new numeric defect identified.

domains.checked: Cisplatin 100 mg/m² every 21 days for three cycles with radiotherapy. Same-day RT sequencing and cancellation guards apply. ECOG 0–2 and hearing/pregnancy/lactation/hypersensitivity exclusions are retained. Pre-existing renal impairment is a caution here, unlike the 00385 exclusion. FBC, renal and liver profiles at baseline and each cycle; audiology/clearance when indicated.

ANC ≥1.5 AND platelets ≥100: 100%; ANC 1–1.49 OR platelets 75–99: 75%; ANC <1 OR platelets <75: delay chemoradiation, coordinating the RT decision. Printed fractional gaps require review. Renal 40–49, 50–59, <40 and dialysis branches remain distinct. Grade 2 neuropathy: 25% reduction; grade 3/4: omit.

Hydration/electrolytes and oral hydration encouragement for 24 hours; dentistry and nutrition consultation before treatment. Assess hearing and sensory symptoms before each cycle; fever requires prompt assessment.

00387.conclusion: Existing v0.84.45 numeric rules retained after fresh-source repeat audit and boundary testing; no new numeric defect identified.

00207.review_date: 2025-01-27 footer last-reviewed date; version 6 dated 2026-09-16, with review as required.

domains.checked: CRC monotherapy requires EGFR-expressing, RAS-wild-type disease and the stated previous-therapy criteria. The head/neck indication is locally advanced disease in patients ineligible for platinum, with RT. Cetuximab 400 mg/m² loading then 250 mg/m² weekly; start one week before RT and continue through RT. Other regimens referencing 00207 for maintenance dosing do not convert this RT patient route into a recurrent/metastatic maintenance service.

ECOG 0–3 and adequate marrow/renal/hepatic function are retained without invented numeric eligibility thresholds. No renal/hepatic/dialysis adjustment is expected. Grade 1/2 infusion reactions require rate/symptom management; grade 3/4 prohibits further treatment. ILD: discontinue. Severe skin recurrence restart rows are 250/200/150 mg/m², with discontinuation after the fourth episode; recovery, the two-week window and prior lower doses remain protected.

Assess antibody-reaction, red-meat allergy and tick-bite history. Baseline/regular bloods, with monthly electrolytes including magnesium and calcium for two months after the last dose. Antihistamine and corticosteroid premedication at least one hour before treatment. Retain the NCCP first-two-infusion versus EMA every-infusion observation discrepancy explicitly for the team.

First-line recurrent/metastatic HNSCC, CPS ≥1 and ECOG 0–2. Up to six 21-day cycles of pembrolizumab 200 mg, carboplatin AUC 5 and fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/day on days 1–4, then pembrolizumab alone every 21 days until progression/toxicity. The 22-hour daily FU schedule and two 48-hour alternative must remain separate. DPD testing before first FU unless already tested; FBC, renal/liver profiles and glucose each cycle; thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks.

Dose levels are carboplatin AUC 5/4/3 then stop and FU 1,000/800/640 then stop. Preserve the conflict between the two-reduction prose and the dose-level table. Treatment-induced ANC <0.5 requires delay/reduction; 0.5–0.99 requires delay. Platelets <50 require delay/reduction; 50–75 requires delay, with the overlapping exact 75 boundary sent for review. Third febrile-neutropenia episode stops platinum. FU bilirubin >85 or AST >180 is contraindicated; equality boundaries require review.

Carboplatin GFR ≤20: do not administer; >20 to ≤30: extreme caution; CrCl <60: higher myelosuppression risk. Cockcroft–Gault/Wright calculation uses a sample within 48 hours. With isotope GFR, a creatinine ratio ≤1.1 may retain the dose; a rise prompts reconsideration. The 00705 severe pembrolizumab organ-impairment advice differs from 00706 and remains separate.

Pneumonitis grade 2: withhold; grade 3/4 or recurrent grade 2: permanently discontinue. Colitis grade 2/3: withhold; grade 4 or recurrent grade 3: stop. Renal/hepatic ULN criteria require attribution. Preserve controlled-endocrine exceptions, ketoacidosis, hypophysitis, SJS/TEN, severe cardiac/neurological toxicity and 12-week recovery/steroid limits. FU hand-foot grade 2 hold differs from grade 3 reduction; mucositis/diarrhoea are FU-specific, whereas increased creatinine affects both cytotoxics.

First-line recurrent/metastatic HNSCC with CPS ≥1. Up to six 21-day combination cycles: pembrolizumab 200 mg, cisplatin 100 mg/m² on day 1, FU 1,000 mg/m²/day on days 1–4; then pembrolizumab alone. FU uses 22-hour daily infusions or two 48-hour infusions as an alternative. Cisplatin runs over two hours with pre/post hydration. Baseline DPD/virology/thyroid/glucose tests and conditional hearing/clearance assessment are retained.

Cisplatin dose levels 100/80/64 and FU 1,000/800/640 remain distinct from organ-function percentages. Retain blood-count and platelet-75 ambiguity handling. Printed cisplatin CrCl 50–59: 75% of original; <50 or dialysis: not recommended. No hepatic cisplatin adjustment is expected. FU bilirubin-85/AST-180 boundaries require review. Pembrolizumab renal/hepatic advice differs from 00705.

Printed immune criteria match the 00705 table, with source-specific provenance. Cisplatin neuropathy ≥grade 2: omit and consider carboplatin. Increased creatinine grade 2–4: hold to recovery, change cisplatin to carboplatin, reduce FU one level. FU-only mucositis, diarrhoea and hand-foot pathways retain component-specific 12-week and dose-reduction limits.

evidence.interpretation: 43 baseline regression scenarios expose five finding groups; they are not 43 distinct clinical defects.

retained_combo.amendment: One documented fractional-CrCl assertion is updated in the execution wrapper; historical files remain unchanged.

limitations: Source reconciliation and software cases do not establish independent clinical or pharmacy approval.
Source-specific differences between the five regimens are retained; no generic organ-function dose bands replace them.
Printed overlaps, gaps and prose/table ambiguities remain explicit Consultant-review pathways.
